question.text: The IMA for Kaveri Infrastructure Fund includes termination provisions. Under which circumstance is for-cause removal of the investment manager by the investors typically supported in the workbook?

answer.text: Premature termination of the manager's services by the investors for default events such as fraud, wilful misconduct, or gross negligence by the manager
When the fund's NAV drops by more than 5% in a single quarter
Whenever 10% of investors request a change in investment manager
At any time without cause, provided 7 days' notice is given

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook supports that an IMA may include termination provisions, and that for-cause removal typically refers to premature termination of the manager's services by investors for default events — mainly fraud, wilful misconduct, and gross negligence by the manager. Disputes arising in this context are addressed at the general level through arbitration or other mutually decided dispute-resolution procedures. NAV fluctuations alone are market-driven and not contractual breaches, a 10% investor threshold is not the supported standard, and a unilateral 7-day no-cause termination would make the manager's mandate commercially unworkable. The Trap: NAV decline appears investor-protective, but market losses are not contractual breaches — only conduct-based defaults like fraud, wilful misconduct, or gross negligence support for-cause manager removal. Note: Rewrote stem, key, and explanation around source-backed for-cause manager removal and the general arbitration/dispute-resolution reference. Removed the unsupported trustee-termination framing, the 30-90 day cure-period, the NAV-drop and 10% investor thresholds, and the seven-day no-cause language.
